card: Reset request ID and JSON-RPC version fields at the beginning of JSONRPCRequest::parse rather than after validating that the request is an object. When handling JSON-RPC batch requests, Bitcoin Core reuses a single request object across elements; non-object elements throw an error before resetting those fields, causing error replies to inherit the preceding request's ID or be dropped if the previous element was a notification. The author supplies a functional test in interface_rpc.py demonstrating both failure modes on master and verifying the fix.
changed_since_previous: No functional changes to the patch or tests since the previous revision; the commit was rebased or re-pushed.
evidence: The PR description demonstrates that for '[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"getblockcount","id":"X"}, 2]', the reply erroneously contains two objects with 'id':'X' (one result and one error).
A new test case added in interface_rpc.py verifies that invalid batch elements do not reuse the previous element's ID and that error replies following a notification are not dropped.
problem: When processing a JSON-RPC batch, the server reuses a single JSONRPCRequest object across each element. If an element is not an object, parse() throws an invalid request exception before resetting id and m_json_version, causing the error reply to reuse the previous element's ID and version, or suppressing the error reply entirely if the preceding call was a JSON-RPC 2.0 notification.

risk.why: A bug in JSON-RPC request parsing could corrupt response payloads or error formatting for clients issuing batch RPC requests.

scope_notes: Small, isolated bug fix in RPC request parsing accompanied by functional test coverage.
summary: Resets the request ID and JSON-RPC version fields at the very beginning of JSONRPCRequest::parse before validating whether the request input is a JSON object. This ensures that non-object elements in a batch request do not inherit the ID and version of the preceding element when generating error replies.
